issues.text: Does not account for hidden Kalshi users trading through Robinhood. Broker-routed Kalshi activity produces no Kalshi descriptor, so those users sit in the control group while actually treated, attenuating the estimate toward zero. Robinhood appears in the merchant dictionary as a descriptor to capture, but the treatment-misclassification consequence is never addressed.
issues.label: blocking
issues.gist: Kalshi users trading via Robinhood produce no Kalshi descriptor, so treated users sit in the control group, attenuating estimates; misclassification never addressed

issues.text: Does not resolve the timing of Kalshi adoption, which is concentrated in specific events and cohorts. Kalshi only ramped its sports contracts around the 2025 football season, so a panel starting Jan 2022 pools politics- and election-driven adopters with sports-driven ones as if they were one population. Cohort-by-calendar-month effects and a robustness spec dropping the Nov 2024 and Jan 2025 cohorts treat this as a nuisance to control for rather than as distinct regimes that should be estimated separately.
issues.label: blocking
issues.gist: Panel from Jan 2022 pools politics/election adopters with post-2025 sports adopters as one population instead of estimating distinct regimes separately

issues.text: Promotional credit is unhandled. Kalshi ran free promos during the sports ramp, so a user can trade without any qualifying bank debit. The treatment definition - first Kalshi debit of $5 or more - will misdate or entirely miss those adopters, mixing treated users back into controls.
issues.label: blocking
issues.gist: Promotional free credit means adopters trade without a qualifying $5 bank debit, so treatment definition misdates or misses them and contaminates controls

critique_prose:
Does not account for hidden Kalshi users trading through Robinhood. Broker-routed Kalshi activity produces no Kalshi descriptor, so those users sit in the control group while actually treated, attenuating the estimate toward zero. Robinhood appears in the merchant dictionary as a descriptor to capture, but the treatment-misclassification consequence is never addressed.

Does not resolve the timing of Kalshi adoption, which is concentrated in specific events and cohorts. Kalshi only ramped its sports contracts around the 2025 football season, so a panel starting Jan 2022 pools politics- and election-driven adopters with sports-driven ones as if they were one population. Cohort-by-calendar-month effects and a robustness spec dropping the Nov 2024 and Jan 2025 cohorts treat this as a nuisance to control for rather than as distinct regimes that should be estimated separately.

Promotional credit is unhandled. Kalshi ran free promos during the sports ramp, so a user can trade without any qualifying bank debit. The treatment definition - first Kalshi debit of $5 or more - will misdate or entirely miss those adopters, mixing treated users back into controls.
